intro.name: The beginning
intro.text:
(Finder) finds a peculiar object under the soil. It has precise edges, unfamiliar materials, and no purpose anyone can identify. One elder calls it a gift; another fears strangers have reached Isola.
{v20_relics}

a1.text: The Shattered Mystery: The object is smashed. Researchers lament the lost evidence; (Finder) is blamed for bringing it.

a2.text: The Thing That Would Not Break: It survives repeated blows and is buried amid fearful rumors.

text_only.reason: rule 9: the buried-relic pool is a state kept across events; no game keeps it

a3.text: The Destruction That Saved Them: An unpleasant odor or startling reaction sends the villagers away; nobody agrees whether the attempt prevented danger or created it.

a4.text: The Accidental Discovery: A useful component inspires a new island-made tool. (Finder) is suddenly praised as an inventor.

b1.text: The Impossible Tool: (Finder) discovers a practical function; craftspeople attempt to imitate it using island materials.

b2.text: The Voice from Nowhere: The object speaks or makes a strange noise; some villagers flee, others pray, and panic spreads.

b3.text: The Hero of the Village: (Finder) uses it to solve a problem without understanding how it works. Public acclaim follows.

b4.text: The Catastrophic Misunderstanding: A ceremony accidentally activates the object, igniting a theological dispute.

c1.text: The Scholar's Triumph: Its construction inspires several practical discoveries. (Finder) is honored.

c2.text: The Great Scholarly Embarrassment: Masters confidently identify it as a ceremonial relic until a child finds its actual use.

c3.text: The Forbidden Question: Scholars propose that distant people possess far greater technology; elders demand silence.

text_only.reason: narrative: 'technology' is part of the story, not a change the event makes

c4.text: The Accused Discoverer: Unfamiliar markings lead villagers to accuse (Finder) of communicating with outsiders.

d1.text: Forgotten Beneath the Earth: The object passes into legend.

text_only.reason: rule 9: the buried-relic pool is a state kept across events; no game keeps it

d2.text: The Second Discoverer: (Second) digs it up years later; an elderly witness cries, "That thing again?!"

d3.text: The Accusation: A witness reports the burial as suspicious. (Finder) must explain (finder.his/her) actions to the elders.

d4.text: The Relic That Returned: The object reappears near the huts; nobody admits moving it. Was it sabotage, chance, or a curse?

coda_p1.text: Reluctant Hero: A destroyer accidentally discovers a useful tool.

coda_p2.text: Disgraced Scholar: A confident expert misidentifies the relic.

coda_p4.text: False Prophet: A claimant of divine authority is exposed.

coda_p5.text: Inventor's Curse: Reproducing a mechanism leads to sorcery accusations.

coda_p6.text: Secret Society: Researchers meet privately to study the objects.

coda_p7.text: The Great Panic: Rumors disrupt work and empty the village stores.

text_only.reason: a large food loss, never below zero
